title: Git Internals, Content-Addressable Storage, DAG & History Rewriting
summary: Master Git internals from content-addressable object databases (blobs, trees, commits, tags) to branch merging, cherry-picking, interactive rebasing, bisect debugging, reflog recovery, and GPG commit verification.
learningObjectives: Inspect Git's content-addressable object store using low-level plumbing commands (hash-object, cat-file, rev-parse).
Perform clean branch isolation, fast-forward and 3-way merges, and selective cherry-picking across release lines.
Reword, squash, and reorder commit histories using interactive rebase while auditing changes through git reflog.
Isolate regression-introducing commits using binary search bisect and sign commits with cryptographic GPG keys.

curriculumModules.title: Content-Addressable Object Database & Plumbing Commands
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Git is fundamentally a content-addressable key-value store with a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) built on top. Objects (blobs, trees, commits, annotated tags) are compressed and addressed strictly by their SHA-1 checksum.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: GitOps engines like ArgoCD and Flux compute tree hashes and commit SHAs to detect configuration drift between cluster desired state and version control repositories.

curriculumModules.title: Branching Strategies, Cherry-Pick, Rebase, Bisect & Reflog
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Branches are lightweight 41-byte movable pointers to commits. Rebasing linearizes release history, cherry-picking ports standalone security patches, and git reflog provides a lossless safety net for HEAD pointer recovery.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Production GitOps pipelines mandate linear commit histories through trunk-based development, automated rebase merges, and signed commits verified via GPG/Cosign before cluster deployment.

labs.title: Git Plumbing: Object Database, Hashing & Tree Inspection
labs.scenario: You are auditing a GitOps repository's internal integrity. You must initialize a git repository in /home/learner/gitops-repo, hash raw Kubernetes manifests into the object database using git hash-object -w, inspect object types and content using git cat-file, stage and commit the files, and verify commit references with git rev-parse.
labs.productionContext: Understanding Git plumbing commands allows platform engineers to debug corrupt GitOps state stores, repair broken refs, and optimize repository packfile performance.
objectives: Initialize an empty Git repository named gitops-repo in /home/learner
Create a pod manifest and write it to the Git object database using git hash-object -w
Stage and commit the manifest to the main branch
Inspect commit tree and metadata using git cat-file and git rev-parse

steps.title: Initialize Git Repository
steps.instruction: Navigate to `/home/learner` and initialize a new git repository in `gitops-repo`.

steps.title: Create and Hash Manifest Object
steps.instruction: Create `pod.yaml` inside `gitops-repo` and write it directly into the object store with `git hash-object -w pod.yaml`.
steps.commandHint: cd /home/learner/gitops-repo && echo "apiVersion: v1" > pod.yaml && git hash-object -w pod.yaml

steps.title: Stage and Commit Manifest
steps.instruction: Stage `pod.yaml` and record a commit with message `feat: initial pod manifest`.
steps.commandHint: git add pod.yaml && git commit -m "feat: initial pod manifest"

steps.title: Inspect Commit Object and References
steps.instruction: Verify the HEAD commit hash with `git rev-parse HEAD` and inspect the commit object with `git cat-file -p HEAD`.
steps.commandHint: git rev-parse HEAD && git cat-file -p HEAD

validationRules.description: Initialized empty Git repository for GitOps workloads
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git init gitops-repo' to create the repository directory and object database.

validationRules.description: Hashed raw manifest into Git object database with git hash-object -w
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git hash-object -w pod.yaml' to compute the SHA-1 object hash and store it in .git/objects/.

validationRules.description: Staged and committed manifest to main branch
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git add pod.yaml && git commit -m "feat: initial pod manifest"' to commit the manifest.

validationRules.description: Inspected object database structure using git cat-file -p
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git cat-file -p HEAD' to inspect the tree and metadata of the commit object.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure you initialize gitops-repo, hash pod.yaml with -w, commit changes, and inspect HEAD with git cat-file -p.

labs.title: Git Advanced Workflows: Cherry-Pick, Rebase, Bisect & Reflog Recovery
labs.scenario: A critical security fix was committed to feature/auth that must be cherry-picked to main. Next, feature branches must be rebased onto main to maintain a clean linear GitOps history, regression commits must be traced using git bisect, and history movements must be audited using git reflog.
labs.productionContext: Advanced Git fluency is mandatory for GitOps platform teams handling hotfixes across production clusters, resolving merge conflicts, and maintaining audited change logs.
objectives: Create branch feature/auth and commit an authentication fix
Cherry-pick the fix commit onto the main branch
Rebase feature branch changes onto main for linear history
Inspect HEAD movement history with git reflog and run git bisect session

steps.title: Create Feature Branch and Commit Fix
steps.instruction: Initialize or navigate to `/home/learner/gitops-repo`, create branch `feature/auth`, switch to it, add `auth.yaml`, and commit with message `fix(sec): patch auth bypass`.
steps.commandHint: cd /home/learner && git init gitops-repo && cd gitops-repo && git branch feature/auth && git checkout feature/auth && echo "security: hardened" > auth.yaml && git add auth.yaml && git commit -m "fix(sec): patch auth bypass"

steps.title: Cherry-Pick Fix onto Main
steps.instruction: Switch back to `main` and cherry-pick the latest commit from `feature/auth`.
steps.commandHint: git checkout main && git cherry-pick feature/auth

steps.title: Rebase onto Main
steps.instruction: Rebase changes onto `main` to preserve a linear history.

steps.title: Audit History with Reflog and Bisect
steps.instruction: Inspect HEAD movements with `git reflog` and initialize a `git bisect` session.
steps.commandHint: git reflog && git bisect start && git bisect bad && git bisect reset

validationRules.description: Created feature branch feature/auth for hotfix development
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git branch feature/auth' to create the isolated development branch.

validationRules.description: Cherry-picked security commit onto main branch
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git checkout main && git cherry-pick feature/auth' to graft the commit onto main.

validationRules.description: Rebased branch onto main to ensure linear GitOps history
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git rebase main' to replay commits onto current main branch.

validationRules.description: Audited HEAD reference movements using git reflog
validationRules.remediation: Run 'git reflog' to inspect previous HEAD pointer history.

solutionCommands: cd /home/learner && git init gitops-repo && cd gitops-repo
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure you create feature/auth, commit to it, cherry-pick to main, rebase main, and check git reflog.

assessmentQuestions.question: What four core immutable object types form the foundation of Git's content-addressable database in .git/objects/?
options: blobs, trees, commits, and annotated tags
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Git's internal object database contains four core object types: blobs (file contents), trees (directory structures with modes and filenames), commits (commit metadata with tree and parent pointers), and annotated tags (cryptographic or annotated pointers).

assessmentQuestions.question: How does `git reflog` differ from `git log` during incident recovery?
options: `git reflog` records all local HEAD movements (including resets, rebases, and deleted commits), whereas `git log` only traverses reachable commit ancestors in the current DAG
`git reflog` requires network access to the remote server, while `git log` is strictly local
`git reflog` compresses git packfiles, whereas `git log` parses commit messages
`git reflog` only tracks changes made by the root user
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Git reflog (reference log) records every time HEAD changes position locally (commits, checkouts, resets, cherry-picks), enabling recovery of orphaned commits even after destructive commands like `git reset --hard`.
